newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 11.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS-factors to watch - Sept 11.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Wednesday morning.
** Parliament to debate the 1996/97 (April-March) budget proposals. Finance Minister expected to take the floor
** Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda says to liberalise industrial sectors to achieve foreign direct investment of $10 billion annually, the Financial Express reports
** Financial institutions to dispose off their stakes in poorly performing companies, will debar promoters from bidding for the stock, the Economic Times says
** The central bank governor says interest rates are likely to soften as inflation remain under control, the Business Line reports
** The National Stock Exchange revamps its 50-stock index replacing six stocks effective September 18
** The spot dollar/rupee INR= opened little changed at 35.72/74 per dollar and seen quiet, dealers say
** On Tuesday, Indian shares drifted lower after the government stuck to a controversial minimum tax on firms which analysts say will squeeze profits and affect high-growth companies
** The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index closed 33.46 points, or 0.96 percent, lower at 3,434.83
** The 100-share National index fell 16.60 points, or 1.06 percent, to 1,547.02
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange index dropped 13 points, or 1.28 percent, to 1,001
** The Delhi share index fell 9.07 points to 766.99
** The Calcutta index .CALSN fell 2.76 points to 442.90
** The Madras index .MDSI slid 13.33 points to 3,491.66
** The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR Index JCEAI eased 1.89 points, or 2.62 percent, to 70.49 with the premium over the local market at 11.25 percent against Monday's 12.29 percent
